name: Komi-Zyrian
confidence_why: Itkonen 1955 and Lytkin 1970 agree that in Komi-Yazva stress falls on the first syllable with a non-high vowel and on the last syllable when every vowel is high, but that is the Yazva lect (listed by Glottolog as a separate language), and Lytkin 1970 describes Komi-Zyrian proper as having free stress with only a tendency toward the first syllable, so the rule is secure for Yazva and does not describe Komi-Zyrian as a whole.

Der Akzent, der hier erscheint, ist beweglich und die Betonung hängt vom Öffnungsgrade der Vokale ab. ... Im Sinne dieser Terminologie sind die Vertreter der urpermischen Vokale u, i̮ und i als «leicht» zu bezeichnen, wogegen die übrigen «schwer» sind. Der Akzent ist gewöhnlich in der Silbe zu finden, die den ersten «schweren» Vokal hat. Gibt es nur «leichte» Vokale im Worte, so ist das Wort endbetont. ... audit.action: check whether this is the same language as another entry
audit.recode_to: Split: move the present Itkonen 1955:28-29 / Lytkin 1961 vowel-quality ('leftmost heavy = non-high vowel, else final') record to komi1277 Komi-Yazva; code komi1268 Komi-Zyrian as quantity-insensitive initial stress, weak/non-obligatory (Lytkin 1970:248 'тенденция ставить ударение на первый слог, однако это необязательно'; Estill 2006:75-76 94.6-97.6% initial in read speech; Itkonen 1955:29-30; LES 1990), with a note on dialectal stem/suffix-conditioned deviations (Izhma minimal pairs pemda· ~ pe·mda, Itkonen 1955:30; Luza-Letka -ал attraction, Lytkin 1970:251). Not weight-sensitive, not unbounded.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim in the Itkonen 1955 file we hold at pp. 28-29 (text ll. 389-431 and the p. 29 page scan). (2) But the passage describes 'Ostpermjakisch' = Komi-Yazva, which Glottolog 5.x lists as a separate language komi1277 (checked on glottolog.org); the StressTyp2 entry for this language 'Yazva' and WALS 'yzv' were inherited under language 766 Komi-Zyrian and the roster key komi1268, and the the compilers flagged this in the current catalog, yet the public record is named 'Komi-Zyrian' with a weight-sensitive unbounded rule. Every source opened for Komi-Zyrian proper says otherwise: Itkonen 1955:29-30 (same copies we hold) treats 'die eigentliche Komi-Sprache' separately (varied; stem stress in some dialects); Lytkin 1970:248 (downloaded now, open, page scan read) says Komi-Zyrian has only a tendency to initial stress and the speaker may stress any syllable; Estill 2006 (held, unused) measures 9

sources.citation: Lytkin, V. I. 1970. Проблема лексического ударения в финно-угорских языках [The problem of lexical stress in the Finno-Ugric languages]. Acta Linguistica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 20(3-4): 245-263. Open whole-volume scan, REAL-J MTAKhttps://real-j.mtak.hu/823/1/ACTALINGV_20.pdf
sources.quote: p. 248: 'В коми-зырянском языке имеется тенденция ставить ударение на первый слог, однако это необязательно: говорящий произвольно может ставить на любой слог даже при изолированном произношении слова: ко́кьямыс~кокья́мыс 'восемь', ве́тымын~веты́мын~ветымы́н 'пятьдесят', ко́травны~котра́вны~котравны́ 'бегать'.' (Komi-Zyrian grouped with Erzya as 'absolutely free' stress with an initial tendency). p. 250: 'Идеальным примером, где место ударения зависит от фонетического фактора, является коми-язьвинский диалект. В неодносложных словах этого диалекта ударение не падает на гласные исконно верхнего
sources.locator: p. 248 (Komi-Zyrian; p. 270 of the volume, page scan read); p. 250 (Komi-Yazva; p. 272); p. 251 (Luza/Letka dialect suffix -ал attraction); pp. 261-262 (Komi 'лишь тенденция ставить акцент на 1-й слог'; Komi-Zyrian 'отчасти' absolutely free)
sources.note: Lytkin's own typology: Komi-Zyrian = initial tendency, non-obligatory, speaker may stress any syllable (p. 248); Komi-Yazva = 'quality-vocalic' stress (p. 250). Directly separates the two lects the record conflates.

sources.note: The primary first-hand description of the Komi-Yazva vowel-quality stress rule that this record actually codes; we hold only Itkonen's 1955 second-hand summary and Normanskaja's 2018 restatement. Needed for the re-keyed komi1277 record (and to settle the 'else final' vs 'next syllable' wording: Itkonen says endbetont, Lytkin 1970:250 says 'на каком-нибудь гласном непервого слога').
